land.text: the land Yao Chang held after leaving Former Qin; the pages give no extent

predecessors.note: Chang'an itself came in 386, from Western Yan.

land.text: Jin forces entered Guanzhong and Luoyang in 416-417

successors.note: The Chang'an region passed to Xia soon after (undated on the Emperor Wu page); Cliopatria's Jin row is Western Jin 265-425, which carries the Eastern Jin.

capitals.name: Chang'an (Xi'an)
capitals.note: Infobox lists Chang'an; "In 386, Yao Chang occupied the city". Where Yao Chang sat in 384-385 the pages do not say.

rulers.name: Yao Chang
rulers.note: Everlasting King of Qin 384; emperor 386; the page has him die in 394.

correction.text: the Cliopatria 387 shape carried back to 384-385; the pages give no extent

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Yao Chang takes the title Everlasting King of Qin in 384 ("taking the title of Everlasting King of Qin and proclaiming a new reign era in 384") but Cliopatria starts in 387. No page opened gives the extent in 384-385; the 387 shape (the north-Shaanxi and Pingyang land) is carried back as a bridge.

correction.text: the 387 shape plus Chang'an and Guanzhong, occupied in 386

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: "In 386, Yao Chang occupied the city [Chang'an], where he elevated himself to Emperor of (Later) Qin." Cliopatria's 387 shape does not contain Chang'an (0 of 14 cells at a 30 km disc) and gives it to Former Qin until 393.

correction.text: the 387 shape plus Chang'an and Guanzhong, held from 386

keyframe_review.note: 110,401 km2 for 387-393, without Chang'an. The Later Qin page: Yao Chang occupied Chang'an in 386, and the stalemate with Former Qin ended with the victory at Dajie in 389; the Former Qin page leaves Fu Deng at Nan'an. The Former Qin shape of the same years (Cliopatria) also contains Chang'an. The page gives no infobox area to compare.

minus.text: Henan: Eastern Jin land and Later Yan land until Luoyang fell to Later Qin in 399

correction.text: the 394 shape without Henan until the 399 capture of Luoyang

keyframe_review.note: 323,956 km2 for 394: the Former Qin remnants added, but the shape also holds half of Henan (Zhengzhou, Jiaozuo, Luoyang), whereas the page has Later Qin capture "Luoyang and nearby commanderies" only in 399 and the Western Yan page has Murong Yong's attempt on Luoyang fail against Eastern Jin. Henan removed until 399.

minus.text: Henan: Eastern Jin land and Later Yan land until Luoyang fell to Later Qin in 399

correction.text: the 395 shape without Henan until the 399 capture of Luoyang

keyframe_review.note: 324,455 km2, the same outline as 394; same repair (Henan removed until 399).

minus.text: Henan: Eastern Jin land and Later Yan land until Luoyang fell to Later Qin in 399

correction.text: the 397 shape without Henan until the 399 capture of Luoyang

keyframe_review.note: 323,512 km2 for 397-401, same outline; Henan removed for 397-398 and restored by the 399 ledger gain of Luoyang and its commanderies.

489,923 km2: adds Longxi and Tianshui (Western Qin conquered "in 400"), Luoyang and Henan (399), and Ningxia. Hexi is absent although Later Liang surrendered "its territory in 403" (ledger 403). Hebei 21 % of its cells looks like polygon noise; unverified, no page names Hebei land. No infobox area is given. (unverified: page budget)

573,288 km2 for 407-409, the peak: Wuwei (Hexi) now inside, consistent with the 403 surrender of Later Liang and "in 405, Chouchi also submitted, bringing Later Qin to its peak". The 407 submissions of Southern Yan and Western Shu are vassalages outside the shape. No infobox area to compare. Outline beyond the places named is unverified: page budget.

460,712 km2 for 410-413: Longxi and Tianshui gone, matching "That year [409], Qifu Gangui restored the Western Qin" and the return of the capital to Yuanchuan with several Later Qin commanderies captured in 410. Wuwei still inside; the page says Yao Xing gave Hexi to Southern Liang, undated, and the Northern Liang page has Guzang as its capital from 412, so the shape holds it a year or two too long.

332,280 km2 for 414-416: Hexi and the Ordos (Tongwan) gone, Luoyang still inside until the winter of 416. The Ordos loss to Xia is undated on the pages ("Helian Bobo rebelled in the Ordos"). Unverified beyond that. The state ends 417, not 416. Outline beyond the places named is unverified: page budget.

correction.text: the Chang'an region, all that remained after Luoyang fell in winter 416

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the end year 417: Luoyang fell in winter 416 and "in spring 417 ... Wang Zhen'e's fleet then arrived and defeated Later Qin's final resistance, entering Chang'an"; Yao Hong surrendered. What remains in 417 is the Guanzhong round the capital.

region.text: the Cliopatria 387 shape as a bridge; the pages give no extent for 384

ledger.note: 384: Yao Chang rebels against Former Qin and takes the title Everlasting King of Qin. "taking the title of Everlasting King of Qin and proclaiming a new reign era in 384" (infobox: founded 384). The Former Qin page lists Yao Chang's Later Qin among the revolts that followed Fei River.

386: Yao Chang occupies Chang'an and proclaims himself emperor. "In 386, Yao Chang occupied the city, where he elevated himself to Emperor of (Later) Qin." Western Yan had captured Chang'an in 385 and "abandoned" it in 386 for Zhangzi (Western Yan page), so the counterpart is the departing Western Yan; Fu Jiān had been executed by Yao Chang on 16 October 385.
386: Chang'an becomes the Later Qin capital. The infobox lists Chang'an without a date; the text ties Yao Chang's control of it to 386.

region.text: Fu Deng's Former Qin remnant; no page locates the battles

ledger.note: 386: Later Qin and Fu Deng's Former Qin face each other. Fu Deng was acclaimed emperor in 386; the Later Qin page speaks of a stalemate ended by "the Battle of Dajie in 389" but gives no start. Page silent on where the fighting was; the year is bridged.

region.text: Fu Deng's Former Qin remnant without Henan

ledger.note: 394: the Former Qin is destroyed. Fu Deng "suffered a major defeat at the Battle of Dajie in 389, and in 394 his forces were destroyed at the Battle of Feiqiao. Yao Xing then executed him."; Fu Chong fled to Huangzhong and was killed by Western Qin forces. Yao Chang died and Yao Xing succeeded in 394 (Later Qin page). The region is Cliopatria's Former Qin 392 shape; the pages do not describe the remnant's land.
394: the Former Qin ends at Feiqiao.

399: Later Qin takes Luoyang from Eastern Jin. "in 399, they capitalized on Eastern Jin's internal turmoil to capture" Luoyang and nearby commanderies; Yao Xing changed his title to Heavenly King that year. Cliopatria's Jin row is Western Jin 265-425, which carries the Eastern Jin.

region.text: Western Qin: Longxi and the upper Wei and Yellow River valleys

ledger.note: 400: Later Qin conquers Western Qin. "In 400, they conquered Western Qin." The Western Qin page tells it differently: Gangui, "heavily defeated", surrendered to Southern Liang and later fled to Later Qin, which made him a general and let him keep his former territory; the state was restored in 409.

401: Later Liang submits after the siege of Guzang. "forced the Later Liang into submission after besieging their capital" (Later Qin page, 401); the Later Liang page: Lü Long was made "Duke of Jiankang" as a vassal, with no exact year for the siege.
403: Lü Long surrenders the whole territory. "Lü Long surrendered the entire territory to Later Qin and moved to Chang'an, ending the Later Liang."

region.text: the Later Liang territory: Guzang (Wuwei) and the Hexi corridor

ledger.note: 403: Later Qin annexes the Later Liang. "The Later Liang surrendered their territory in 403." Cliopatria draws Hexi as Later Qin only from 407 and keeps a Later Liang shape to 406.

region.text: Chouchi, a Di state in southern Gansu; the Later Qin page does not locate it

ledger.note: 405: Chouchi submits to Later Qin. "in 405, Chouchi also submitted, bringing Later Qin to its peak." The region is the researcher's reading; the page does not say when the relation ended, so it is left open to the end of the state in 417.

region.text: Southern Yan, the Murong state in Shandong

ledger.note: 407: Southern Yan and Western Shu submit. "In 407, he received Southern Yan and Western Shu's submissions." Helian Bobo rebelled in the Ordos in the same period (the page does not date it).

region.text: Longxi, where "the Western Qin was revived"

ledger.note: 409: Qifu Gangui restores the Western Qin. "In 409, the Western Qin was revived in the Longxi," reducing Later Qin's territory; the Western Qin page restores it at Mount Dujian in 409, returns the capital to Yuanchuan in 410 and has it capture "several Later Qin commanderies".

region.text: Southern Yan, the Murong state in Shandong

ledger.note: 410: Southern Yan falls to Liu Yu. "In 409 ... Liu Yu also launched his campaign against Southern Yan"; Southern Yan fell "leading to Southern Yan's demise in 410" (Emperor Wu of Liu Song page: "In spring 410, Liu Yu captured Guanggu, ending Southern Yan").

412: Later Qin's Hexi holdings pass out of its hands. Page silent on the year: "Yao Xing gave up his Hexi holdings to Southern Liang" is undated; the Northern Liang page shows Guzang as the Northern Liang capital 412-439 (the page of Later Qin does not mention Northern Liang). Cliopatria drops Wuwei in 414. Bridged to 412.

414: the Ordos is gone to Xia. Page silent on the year: it says only that Helian Bobo "rebelled in the Ordos" (the infobox gives 407). Cliopatria's Later Qin shape drops Tongwan in 414 and its Xia shape grows that year.
416: Luoyang falls to Liu Yu. "In 416, Liu Yu launched a major attack against Later Qin." "In winter 416, the important city Luoyang fell to Liu Yu's general Tan Daoji."

417: Jin forces enter Chang'an and Yao Hong surrenders. "Wang Zhen'e's fleet then arrived and defeated Later Qin's final resistance, entering Chang'an" (spring 417). Liu Yu then returned to Jiankang; Liu Yizhen's forces were defeated by Xia at Qingni and "the Chang'an region became Xia possession, although Jin retained the Luoyang region" (undated).

region.text: the Chang'an region, the last Later Qin land

ledger.note: 417: the Later Qin ends. "by late 417, Yao Shao had died while Jin forces entered the Guanzhong and reached Chang'an." Yao Hong was executed in Jiankang. The infobox gives the end as 20 September 417.

wars.name: Later Qin-Former Qin war
wars.outcome: Stalemate until "the crucial victory at the Battle of Dajie in 389"; Fu Deng's forces destroyed at Feiqiao in 394; Fu Chong killed by Western Qin forces.
wars.note: No page locates Dajie or Feiqiao.

wars.name: Later Qin conquest of Western Qin
wars.outcome: Gangui heavily defeated and surrendered to Southern Liang, later fled to Later Qin; the state revived in 409.

wars.name: Later Qin subjugation of Later Liang
wars.outcome: Guzang besieged 401, Lü Long a vassal, and the whole territory surrendered in 403.

wars.name: Battle of Chaibi
wars.outcome: "a heavy defeat to the Northern Wei at the Battle of Chaibi in 402", halting eastward expansion; no land change on the pages.

wars.name: Restoration of Western Qin
wars.outcome: Gangui restored the Western Qin in 409 and captured several Later Qin commanderies in 410.

wars.name: Liu Yu's conquest of Later Qin
wars.outcome: Luoyang fell in winter 416, Chang'an in spring 417; Yao Hong surrendered; Xia then took the Chang'an region from Liu Yizhen at Qingni (undated).

certainty.note: Every frontier is approximate: the Former Qin remnant, Eastern Jin, Wei and the Hexi states. No treaty line is on any page opened.

notes: Cliopatria's Later Qin row 387..416 starts three years late and ends a year early (384..417). Its 387-393 shape lacks Chang'an, which the Later Qin page dates to 386; its 394-401 shapes hold half of Henan, which the page gives to Later Qin only in 399 (Luoyang). Cliopatria's Former Qin shapes of 387-393 also contain Chang'an; see the former-qin dossier. Hexi appears in the shape only in 407 although the page dates the Later Liang surrender 403. The Ordos loss (to Xia) and the Hexi loss (to Southern Liang or Northern Liang) are undated on the Later Qin page and recorded at confidence 1. The Later Qin page gives no infobox area, so no area comparison could be made (Cliopatria's maximum is 573,288 km2). Not settled: where Yao Chang was in 384-385; the Chouchi and Western Shu relations (Western Shu's submission of 407 is on the page; its end is not, so it carries no event and Western Shu needs a dossier; counterpart slug western-shu, around 405-413); Helian Bobo's rebellion (page gives 407 in the infobox and no year in the text); the Battle of Chaibi (page 'Battle of Chaibi' did not load; cited from the Later Qin page). Counterparts without a dossier: chouchi, western-shu. The Western Qin page and the Later Qin page differ on 400: conquest of Western Qin against Gangui's surrender to Southern Liang and flight to Later Qin; both are noted at the event.
